newsitem.title: USA: AMEX says to trade all options in sixteenths.
newsitem.headline: AMEX says to trade all options in sixteenths.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange said Wednesday its systems will be ready to process all options trades in minimum increments of 1/16th of a dollar by July 28.
The move follows the exchange's adoption on May 7 of trading all equities in increments of 1/16th or $0.625, a departure from the past practice of trading in intervals of 1/8 or $0.125.
Currently, only options priced below $3 are traded in 1/16ths on the AMEX.
AMEX said while its trading systems will be ready for the interval change on options by July 28, it was still awaiting industry concensus and approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission.

"We are ready to go when the industry in a position to make this change, but there needs to be cooperation within the options industry in order for investors to truly benefit," said AMEX Chairman Richard Syron.
The move to trade on 1/16th intervals is seen as a step that eventually will lead Wall Street to trade in decimals instead of fractions.
The New York Stock Exchange began trading stocks in 1/16ths increments of 1/16th on June 24.
